meta.guide_tau: Level caption:  energy (NIST, or a measurement of the last 20 years where one exists) and measured lifetime (where one exists).
meta.notes: Isotope shifts are nu(A) - nu(40), in MHz; for 43Ca they refer to the hyperfine centre of gravity. Frequencies refer to 40Ca. Hyperfine A, B follow the usual convention (43Ca has a negative nuclear moment, mu = -1.317643 mu_N, I = 7/2). Extra (non-schema) fields used: linewidth_Hz / linewidth_kHz / linewidth_MHz (natural linewidth, FWHM, as printed), wavelength_vac_nm, zeeman, note, alternatives (other measurements of the same quantity), top-level ionization and photoionization blocks. Lifetimes marked 'compilation' are the experimental values collected in Table 1 of Den Hartog et al. 2021 (laser-based methods only), which was read from a rendered image of the arXiv PDF because its text layer drops digits. The NIST Ca I levels file has no Lande-g column; the two measured g_J values given here are the only ones found. The 1D2 -> 3P1,2 rates (300 and 96 s^-1) and the 1D2 total lifetime are poorly known: experiment 1.5(4) ms versus theory 1.71 ms, while 300 + 96 + 40 s^-1 would give 2.3 ms.
